description: Replace the low-batch n=2048/4096 graph DAG with coarse per-matrix cooperative clusters rather than global task stealing: assign stable factor, panel, and update roles inside each cluster, keep 128-column epochs and panels resident, and expose only stage-level device barriers with next-diagonal lookahead.

Replaced global cooperative task stealing with stable interleaved per-matrix clusters: each resident CTA keeps one matrix owner and local worker index across factor, panel solve, and triangular Schur stages, with only stage-level grid barriers. Full validation and fresh-input guards passed. Full-grid metric 839.741071 us; b8/n2048=2996.226 us and b2/n4096=4991.846 us, versus same-run 148-CTA global assignment 2854.850/4827.850 us.

Changed stable cooperative residency from 148 to 144 CTAs so both batch-8 and batch-2 targets receive equal-sized matrix clusters while preserving fixed roles and stage barriers. Full validation and fresh-input guards passed. Full-grid metric 848.198562 us; b8/n2048=3087.187 us and b2/n4096=5242.930 us, slower than the 148-CTA stable-cluster trial at 2996.226/4991.846 us.

Restored the measured 148-CTA stable-cluster configuration after the 144-CTA balance sweep. Source is the validated Trial0 design and retains fixed per-matrix worker ownership with factor/panel/update stages separated only by cooperative grid barriers. Reuses Trial0 metric 839.741071 us because this commit only restores the exact launch constant; final nsys was attempted on b2/n4096 but the graph-range harness generated no report, with diagnostics retained in the profile text.

Explored coarse per-matrix cooperative clusters for the low-batch n=2048/4096 device DAG. Started from the same-run 148-CTA cooperative epoch kernel, then replaced global task stealing with stable interleaved clusters: each CTA retains one matrix owner and local worker index through diagonal factor, panel solve, and triangular Schur work, with stage-level grid barriers. The 148-CTA variant passed full validation and fresh-input guards at 839.741071 us overall, b8/n2048=2996.226 us and b2/n4096=4991.846 us, versus the prior global assignment's 839.006179 us and 2854.850/4827.850 us. An evenly divisible 144-CTA sweep also passed but measured 848.198562 us and 3087.187/5242.930 us. Final HEAD restores the 148-CTA stable-cluster design. Final nsys was attempted under the required wrapper; no report was generated and diagnostics are preserved. Concrete openings remain: per-matrix epoch counters or cluster barriers to remove whole-grid synchronization, a dedicated next-diagonal owner that overlaps lookahead with off-diagonal updates, true cluster shared/TMEM panel multicast, and 128x128 tensor-core Schur tiles to reduce task count.

Continue the stable per-matrix cluster foundation by removing whole-grid synchronization: add per-matrix epoch counters or cluster-local barriers, dedicate one next-diagonal owner that advances lookahead while other CTAs execute off-diagonal updates, and increase Schur work to 128x128 tensor-core tiles with shared or TMEM panel multicast to reduce task count.

Continue the stable per-matrix cluster foundation by removing whole-grid synchronization: add per-matrix epoch counters or cluster-local barriers, dedicate one next-diagonal owner that advances lookahead while other CTAs execute off-diagonal updates, and increase Schur work to 128x128 tensor-core tiles with shared or TMEM panel multicast to reduce task count.

Removed whole-grid cooperative synchronization by adding per-matrix arrival counters and generation epochs. Each stable matrix cluster now copies, factors, solves, and updates independently; a cluster's final CTA publishes the next generation after threadfence while other matrices can advance without waiting. Full validation and fresh-input guards passed. Full-grid metric improved from 839.741071 to 832.106559 us; b8/n2048 improved 2996.226 to 2692.970 us and b2/n4096 improved 4991.846 to 4575.829 us.

Dedicated cluster worker 0 to update and immediately factor the next diagonal tile inside the current Schur epoch, removing the following factor barrier while other stable workers process off-diagonal tiles. Official validation and fresh-input guards passed, and b2/n4096 reached 4284.424 us, but the full benchmark exposed a b8/n2048 reconstruction failure (relative residual 0.00576), showing that the static triangular task mapping does not always assign the next diagonal task to worker 0. Logged as runtime failure; all metrics are N/A by schema.

Reserved triangular task zero exclusively for cluster worker 0 and striped all remaining Schur tasks across workers 1..N, ensuring the intended next-diagonal owner actually executes lookahead. Official validation and fresh-input guards passed; b2/n4096 reached 4057.756 us, but the full benchmark again exposed a b8/n2048 reconstruction failure (relative residual 0.00666). The remaining race is specific to the uneven 148-CTA/batch-8 cluster partition, so this lookahead schedule is logged as a runtime failure.

Used 144 resident CTAs for batch-8 so every matrix receives exactly 18 workers while retaining 148 CTAs for batch-2 lookahead. Official validation and fresh-input guards passed, and b2/n4096 measured 4024.268 us, but b8/n2048 still failed reconstruction (relative residual 0.00501). Equal cluster sizes did not remove the dependency violation in the one-barrier lookahead schedule.

Restored the validated per-matrix epoch kernel after three measured next-diagonal lookahead variants exposed b8/n2048 reconstruction failures. This final commit is source-identical to Trial3, passed wrapped build, full validation, and fresh-input guards, and retains Trial3's measured 832.106559 us with b8/n2048=2692.970 us and b2/n4096=4575.829 us. Final nsys was attempted on b2/n4096 but generated no report; diagnostics are retained.

Continued the stable-cluster brief by replacing every whole-grid sync with per-matrix arrival counters and generation epochs. Each matrix cluster now copies, factors, solves, and updates independently; this passed all checks and improved the full metric from 839.741071 to 832.106559 us, b8/n2048 from 2996.226 to 2692.970 us, and b2/n4096 from 4991.846 to 4575.829 us. Three next-diagonal-owner variants then fused task-zero Schur update with POTRF, removed the following factor barrier, reserved task zero to worker 0, and tested equal 18-worker batch-8 clusters. They passed official validation and reduced b2/n4096 to 4284.424, 4057.756, and 4024.268 us, but each failed the full b8/n2048 reconstruction gate at residuals 0.00576, 0.00666, and 0.00501; those failures are committed and logged. Final HEAD restores the validated per-matrix epoch winner. Final nsys again generated no report. Concrete openings remain: a dependency counter for the next diagonal that waits for all contributions to that tile before fused POTRF, a two-level cluster barrier separating diagonal-ready from off-diagonal completion, and a native 128x128 tcgen05 Schur primitive with DSM/TMEM multicast; the current 64x64 MathDx shared footprint cannot hold four accumulators plus multicast panels without a distinct kernel design.

Continue the per-matrix cluster objective with correctness-complete next-diagonal contribution counters. Separate diagonal-ready from stage-complete barriers, wait for every Schur contribution before fused POTRF, and prototype 128x128 tcgen05 updates without returning to whole-grid synchronization.
